# Command reference

<!-- Generated by docs/gen-reference.sh from `quire --help`; do not edit. -->

Every command's `--help`. The options `--lib`, `--library`, `--config` and `-v` work
with every command.

## quire

```text
A reference manager: projects, DOI/arXiv/PubMed/URL lookup, .bib export

Usage: quire [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  tui          Browse the library in the terminal
  add          Add references by DOI, arXiv ID, PMID, PMCID or URL (= `ref add`)
  list         List references as a table (= `ref list`)
  show         Show one reference (= `ref show`)
  ref          Work with references: add, list, show, edit, refetch, check, link, unlink, rm, restore, copy
  tag          Tags on references: add, rm, list, rename, delete, color
  note         Notes on references or standalone: add, list, show, edit, rm
  search       Search the library: metadata, tags, notes, highlights and papers' text
  sync         Keep this library the same on your devices (directly, over QUIC)
  highlight    Passages highlighted in the reader: list (as Markdown quotes), comment, remove
  pdf          PDFs: get (download), import, list, open, path, rm
  project      Work with projects: new, list, tree, rename, rm
  import       Import a .bib file
  export       Write references as BibLaTeX, BibTeX, CSL-JSON or Hayagriva; keep files updated
  folder       Link this folder to a project: quire.toml (new, show)
  library      Work with libraries: new, list, use, rename, rm
  init         Create the library and set your contact email (asked for by Crossref and NCBI)
  config       Read or change settings
  serve        Local endpoint for a browser extension (save the page or PDF you are viewing)
  completions  Print a shell completion script
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --lib <NAME>      Use this registered library [env: QUIRE_LIB]
      --library <PATH>  Use the library in this folder, registered or not [env: QUIRE_LIBRARY]
      --config <FILE>   Config file (default: ~/.config/quire/config.toml) [env: QUIRE_CONFIG=]
  -v, --verbose         Show debug logs (requests, database)
  -h, --help            Print help
  -V, --version         Print version
```

## quire add

```text
Add references by DOI, arXiv ID, PMID, PMCID or URL (= `ref add`)

Usage: quire add [OPTIONS] [INPUTS]...

Arguments:
  [INPUTS]...  DOI, arXiv ID, PMID, PMCID or URL (several allowed)

Options:
      --lib <NAME>         Use this registered library [env: QUIRE_LIB]
  -p, --project <PROJECT>  Put the references into this project, e.g. `thesis/chapter-2`
      --from <FILE>        Also read inputs from this file, one per line
      --library <PATH>     Use the library in this folder, registered or not [env: QUIRE_LIBRARY]
      --config <FILE>      Config file (default: ~/.config/quire/config.toml) [env: QUIRE_CONFIG=]
      --retry              Also retry every earlier failed lookup (see `quire ref check`)
      --forget-failed      Forget every earlier failed lookup instead of adding anything
  -v, --verbose            Show debug logs (requests, database)
  -h, --help               Print help
```

## quire list

```text
List references as a table (= `ref list`)

Usage: quire list [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --lib <NAME>
          Use this registered library [env: QUIRE_LIB]

  -p, --project <PROJECT>
          Only this project

      --library <PATH>
          Use the library in this folder, registered or not [env: QUIRE_LIBRARY]

  -r, --recursive
          With --project: include its subprojects

      --config <FILE>
          Config file (default: ~/.config/quire/config.toml)
          
          [env: QUIRE_CONFIG=]

  -t, --tag <TAG>
          Only references carrying this tag (repeat for several: all must match)

      --all
          The whole library, even inside a folder with quire.toml

  -v, --verbose
          Show debug logs (requests, database)

      --trash
          Show the trash instead

  -c, --columns <COLUMNS>
          Columns to show, comma-separated

          Possible values:
          - key:       Cite key
          - author:    First creator's family name (+ "et al.")
          - year
          - title
          - type:      Entry type (CSL)
          - container: Journal, book or proceedings title
          - doi
          - id:        Reference ID (ref_…)
          - pdf:       PDF: ✓ pages, blocked, not found, no DOI, error, – (never tried; `quire pdf get`)
          - tags:      Tags (colored ones in their color)
          - flags:     Marks: ! = metadata errors, ~ = warnings (see `ref check`), T = in the trash

      --json
          Print JSON (one array of references)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## quire ref

```text
Work with references: add, list, show, edit, refetch, check, link, unlink, rm, restore, copy

Usage: quire ref [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  add         Add references by DOI, arXiv ID, PMID, PMCID or URL
  list        List references as a table
  show        Show one reference
  link        Put references into a project
  unlink      Take references out of a project (they stay in the library)
  rm          Move references to the trash
  restore     Take references out of the trash
  relate      Mark two references as related (both ways)
  unrelate    Remove the relation between two references
  copy        Copy references to another library (same ID there)
  abstracts   Fill in missing abstracts (Europe PMC, else the PDF)
  check       Report metadata issues and failed lookups
  refetch     Look references up again; fields you edited are kept
  edit        Edit a reference in your editor (as TOML)
  duplicates  List references that look like the same work (preprint and journal version, …)
  merge       Merge duplicates into one reference (the others go to the trash)
  distinct    Record that two references are not duplicates
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --lib <NAME>      Use this registered library [env: QUIRE_LIB]
      --library <PATH>  Use the library in this folder, registered or not [env: QUIRE_LIBRARY]
      --config <FILE>   Config file (default: ~/.config/quire/config.toml) [env: QUIRE_CONFIG=]
  -v, --verbose         Show debug logs (requests, database)
  -h, --help            Print help
```

## quire tag

```text
Tags on references: add, rm, list, rename, delete, color

Usage: quire tag [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  add     Put tags on a reference
  rm      Take tags off a reference
  list    List tags with how many references carry each
  rename  Rename a tag (onto an existing name: merge the two)
  delete  Delete a tag from every reference
  color   Color a tag (`none` removes the color): red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, gray or #rrggbb
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --lib <NAME>      Use this registered library [env: QUIRE_LIB]
      --library <PATH>  Use the library in this folder, registered or not [env: QUIRE_LIBRARY]
      --config <FILE>   Config file (default: ~/.config/quire/config.toml) [env: QUIRE_CONFIG=]
  -v, --verbose         Show debug logs (requests, database)
  -h, --help            Print help
```

## quire pdf

```text
PDFs: get (download), import, list, open, path, rm

Usage: quire pdf [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  get      Find and download PDFs (open access, arXiv, publisher pages; --browser for blocked ones)
  import   Attach PDF files, or add the papers they are (by the DOI or arXiv ID they print)
  list     List references with (or without) a PDF
  open     Open a reference's PDF
  path     Print the path of a reference's PDF
  text     Print the paper's text as reader mode shows it (arXiv / Europe PMC full text, else the PDF's)
  extract  Extract papers' text again (after a quire update, or to retry online sources)
  verify   Re-check attached PDFs against their references (DOI or title); changes nothing
  rm       Remove a reference's PDFs (the files stay in the store)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --lib <NAME>      Use this registered library [env: QUIRE_LIB]
      --library <PATH>  Use the library in this folder, registered or not [env: QUIRE_LIBRARY]
      --config <FILE>   Config file (default: ~/.config/quire/config.toml) [env: QUIRE_CONFIG=]
  -v, --verbose         Show debug logs (requests, database)
  -h, --help            Print help
```

### quire pdf get

```text
Find and download PDFs (open access, arXiv, publisher pages; --browser for blocked ones)

Usage: quire pdf get [OPTIONS] [QUERIES]...

Arguments:
  [QUERIES]...  Cite keys, DOIs / arXiv IDs / PMIDs, or reference IDs

Options:
      --lib <NAME>         Use this registered library [env: QUIRE_LIB]
  -p, --project <PROJECT>  Every reference of this project that has no PDF
      --library <PATH>     Use the library in this folder, registered or not [env: QUIRE_LIBRARY]
  -r, --recursive          With --project: include its subprojects
      --blocked            Every reference marked blocked by an earlier `pdf get`
      --config <FILE>      Config file (default: ~/.config/quire/config.toml) [env: QUIRE_CONFIG=]
      --all                Every reference in the library that has no PDF
  -v, --verbose            Show debug logs (requests, database)
      --browser            Try the download first; open only what fails in your browser, one at a time, and attach the PDF you download there
      --direct             With --browser: open publishers' pages directly, not through the proxy (for Cloudflare checks that fail on the proxy, e.g. Wiley; use the publisher's institutional login or a VPN)
      --wait <WAIT>        With --browser: minutes to wait for each download [default: 5]
  -h, --help               Print help
```

## quire export

```text
Write references as BibLaTeX, BibTeX, CSL-JSON or Hayagriva; keep files updated

Usage: quire export [OPTIONS]
       quire export <COMMAND>

Commands:
  auto  List the files kept updated
  stop  Stop keeping a file updated (the file stays)
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --lib <NAME>
          Use this registered library [env: QUIRE_LIB]

      --library <PATH>
          Use the library in this folder, registered or not [env: QUIRE_LIBRARY]

      --config <FILE>
          Config file (default: ~/.config/quire/config.toml)
          
          [env: QUIRE_CONFIG=]

  -p, --project <PROJECT>
          Only this project

  -r, --recursive
          With --project: include its subprojects

  -v, --verbose
          Show debug logs (requests, database)

      --all
          The whole library, even inside a folder with quire.toml

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Write to this file instead of stdout

      --profile <PROFILE>
          Export profile from the config (`[export.<name>]`)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Format (overrides the profile's)

          Possible values:
          - biblatex:  BibLaTeX (Biber)
          - bibtex:    Classic BibTeX
          - csl-json:  CSL-JSON (Pandoc, Zotero)
          - hayagriva: Hayagriva YAML (Typst)

      --keep-updated
          Rewrite the output file after every change from now on

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

```text
      --format <FORMAT>    Format: biblatex, bibtex, csl-json, hayagriva (default: from the file extension)
      --no-keep-updated    Do not keep the bibliography file updated
  -h, --help               Print help
```

## quire library

```text
Work with libraries: new, list, use, rename, rm

Commands:
  new     Create and register a library
  list    List libraries (* = default)

  rename  Rename a library (its folder stays)

  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```

## quire config

```text
Read or change settings

Usage: quire config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  get    Print a value (nothing if unset)
  set    Set a value (lists: comma-separated)
  unset  Remove a value
  list   Print every set value
  keys   Print every key quire knows, with what it does
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --lib <NAME>      Use this registered library [env: QUIRE_LIB]
      --library <PATH>  Use the library in this folder, registered or not [env: QUIRE_LIBRARY]
      --config <FILE>   Config file (default: ~/.config/quire/config.toml) [env: QUIRE_CONFIG=]
  -v, --verbose         Show debug logs (requests, database)
```

## quire serve

```text
Local endpoint for a browser extension (save the page or PDF you are viewing)

Usage: quire serve [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --lib <NAME>      Use this registered library [env: QUIRE_LIB]
      --port <PORT>     Port on 127.0.0.1 [default: 23150]
      --library <PATH>  Use the library in this folder, registered or not [env: QUIRE_LIBRARY]
      --token           Print the access token (to give to the browser extension) and stop
      --config <FILE>   Config file (default: ~/.config/quire/config.toml) [env: QUIRE_CONFIG=]
      --reset-token     Make a new access token (the old one stops working) and stop
  -v, --verbose         Show debug logs (requests, database)
  -h, --help            Print help
```
